svg.title: Who decides what when an AI agent drives harness2 through MCP
svg.desc: The model chooses which tool to call and with which arguments, but cannot write profiles, read secrets, or touch tokens or the audit log, accept host-isolation risk for a person, or exceed its token's role. The MCP server adds one rule of its own, refusing acknowledge_risks unless the person who started it allowed that, and it labels results as untrusted, caps output and bounds waits. The Workbench server decides everything else: each token's role on every call, audited refusals, isolation, validation, limits and budgets.
svg.text: The model chooses
which of 42 tools to call
the arguments, budget_usd too
when to wait and when to stop
It cannot
write profiles, read secrets, or touch
tokens or the audit log: no tool for it
accept host-isolation risk for you
do more than its token's role allows
h2workbench-mcp adds one rule
acknowledge_risks=true is refused unless the person who started it
passed --allow-risk-acknowledgement
and it labels results as untrusted data, caps output near 100 KB, bounds
waits at 600 s, guards its HTTP endpoint and keeps no state
every call forwards the caller's own token
The Workbench server decides
each token's role on every call: viewer < operator < admin
refusals, audited at most 10 a minute per token (the rest counted)
isolation, job validation, limits and budgets
the same rules as for a person
Tokens for agents: viewer by default, operator only to start jobs, never admin.
